title: Where do you live?
goal: Name places, addresses, and where things are — while accepting the second rule that reshapes your sentences: position words stand AFTER the noun.
bekal: use 在 as the verb "to be at" and as a place phrase
put 上面, 裡面, 旁邊 after the noun, not before
give an address in big-to-small order

dialogs.title: 對話 — 找房子
dialogs.intro: Budi wants to move out of the dorm. Xiaomei helps him call about a room for rent.

lines.id: Budi, where are you living now?

lines.speaker: 布迪:
lines.id: In the campus dorm. It's a bit noisy.

lines.text: [樓下|Lóu xià][就|jiù][有|yǒu][一家|yì jiā][小七|Xiǎo Qī]。
lines.literal: floor — below — just — have — one — (measure word) — little-seven.

lines.speaker: 布迪:
lines.text: [聽起來|Tīngqǐlái][很|hěn][不錯|búcuò]。[我|Wǒ][可以|kěyǐ][去|qù][看看|kànkàn][嗎|ma]？

lines.literal: hear-up — very — not — wrong. I — can — go — look-look — (question)?

lines.speaker: 布迪:
lines.text: [謝謝|Xièxie]！[妳|Nǐ][真的|zhēn de][是|shì][我|wǒ][在|zài][台灣|Táiwān][的|de][貴人|guìrén]。
lines.id: Thank you! You're truly my lifesaver in Taiwan.
lines.literal: thank thank! you — truly — (one) — are — I — at — Taiwan — 's — noble-person.

notes: ⚠️ **小七 ("little seven") is the friendly name for 7-Eleven** that everyone in Taiwan uses. Convenience stores in Taiwan are much more than shops: people pay bills, send parcels, buy train tickets, top up their 悠遊卡, and print documents there.
**貴人 ("noble person") means someone who helps you at a key moment** — not a rich person. Calling someone your 貴人 is a warm, sincere compliment, and Taiwanese people are touched to hear it.
**不錯 literally means "not wrong", but it means "pretty good".** It is the most common compliment in Taiwan, more frequent than 很好. Modest, but positive.

**就 (*jiù*) here means "right, just"** — stressing closeness or ease: *樓下就有* ("there's one right downstairs"). This little word is everywhere and hard to translate; get a feel for it rather than looking for a fixed equivalent.
⚠️ **一個月八千 means "eight thousand a month".** Time span first, amount after — no word for "per". The pattern works for everything: *一天三次* (three times a day), *一個星期兩次* (twice a week).

grammars.title: 在: "to be at" and the place phrase
body: **在** does two jobs that English covers with "be at/in". The difference matters: when 在 is the only verb, it means "to be (at)"; when there's another verb, it becomes a place phrase and stands **before** that verb.
after: ⚠️ **我吃飯在家 is the classic English-speaker mistake**, because English says "I eat at home" with the place at the end. Remember the last unit's rule: **all modifiers stand before the verb** — time, place, manner, company. No exceptions at A1.
**Verbs that already contain a sense of place don't need 在**: 住 (live), 去 (go), 來 (come), 回 (return). *我住台北* is complete; *我住在台北* is also right and just as common.

grammars.title: ⚠️ Position words stand AFTER the noun
body: English says "**on** the table" — position first, then the thing. Mandarin flips the order: **thing first, position after**. This reversal takes a while to feel natural.

head: 中文
Pīnyīn
Literally
Meaning
rows: in front of the MRT station

after: The full sentence combines both: **書在桌子上面。** — "The book is on the table." Pattern: thing + 在 + place + position word.
⚠️ **面 and 邊 are often interchangeable** (上面 / 上邊, 裡面 / 裡邊), but in Taiwan **面** is far more common. Some forms have only one option: 旁邊 is always 邊, 中間 always 間.
**After the name of a place, 裡面 can be dropped**: *我在圖書館* ("I'm at the library") doesn't need 裡面. Ordinary objects are what need a position word: *在桌子上面*, not *在桌子*.

blocks.text: ⚠️ **廁所 is the most urgent word to learn.** *請問，廁所在哪裡？* — "Excuse me, where's the restroom?" In Taiwan, clean public restrooms are easiest to find in 捷運站 and 便利商店, and anyone can use them without buying anything.

blocks.title: Five sentences to learn whole
items: **書在桌子上面。** — The book is on the table.
**我家在學校附近。** — My home is near the school.
**廁所在二樓。** — The restroom is on the second floor.
**便利商店在捷運站旁邊。** — The convenience store is next to the MRT station.
**我的錢包在背包裡面。** — My wallet is in my backpack.

sections.title: Addresses: big to small, no exceptions

blocks.text: Taiwanese addresses go from the biggest unit to the smallest — the reverse of the English habit of starting with the house number. The order: **city → district → road → section → lane → number → floor**.

A full address: **台北市大安區忠孝東路四段45巷12號3樓**. Read in order, it narrows down by itself from city to floor. ⚠️ Floors use plain numbers: 三樓 (third floor), 十樓 (tenth floor). And **一樓 is the ground floor** — as in American English, not the British "first floor" above it.

items: Where do you live?
I live in the campus dorm.

The restroom is on the second floor.
Is there a convenience store near here?
